newsitem.title: DUBAI: OPEC chiefs in London talks ahead of quota meeting.
newsitem.headline: OPEC chiefs in London talks ahead of quota meeting.

text.p: OPEC Secretary General Rilwanu Lukman and OPEC President Rakad bin Salem bin Rakad met in London on Sunday ahead of the group's quota compliance meeting on September 25, the UAE news agency WAM reported on Monday.
The two discussed current developments in the oil market and the supply and demand outlook for OPEC oil but gave no other details of their discussions, WAM reported.

The compliance committee meeting in Vienna on Wednesday will be chaired by Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh who, with oil ministers from Nigeria and Libya, will compare official and independent assessments of the group's output.
Analysts say that the group is producing 800,000 barrels per day (bpd) above its agreed supply quota of 25.03 million bpd.

Oil prices have hit five-year highs this month because of renewed tension in the Middle East, unexpected shortfalls in non-OPEC output and and low oil inventory levels ahead of the northern hemisphere's winter.
Aghazadeh has promised a "very specific programme" to deal with overproduction though OPEC sources say little practical will be taken with current strong oil prices.
OPEC holds its main ministerial meeting in November.
